title: Batch Chunk and Window Generators

hidden.label: Window larger than sequence yields empty
Generators work lazily on iterators (not just lists)
hidden.inputDisplay: chunks((x for x in range(7)), 3) and sliding_window((x for x in range(5)), 2)
hidden.script:
assert list(chunks((x for x in range(7)), 3)) == [[0,1,2],[3,4,5],[6]]
assert list(sliding_window((x for x in range(5)), 2)) == [(0,1),(1,2),(2,3),(3,4)]

hidden.label: Size <= 0 raises ValueError
Exact multiple chunk size leaves no extra empty slice

hints: Work with iter(iterable) + itertools.islice OR collections.deque(maxlen=k) so BOTH lists AND lazy single-pass generators work cleanly without calling len().

For chunks(iterable, size): take `batch = list(islice(it, size))` inside `while batch: yield batch`. For sliding_window(iterable, k): fill a `deque(maxlen=k)` with `islice(it, k - 1)` then yield `tuple(win)` as each remaining element enters!

Pseudocode:
  if size <= 0: raise ValueError(...)
  it = iter(iterable)
  while (batch := list(islice(it, size))): yield batch
